# Oil markets are pricing conflict again

* [Geopolitics](https://www.oilandgas360.com/tag/geopolitics/), [Investors](https://www.oilandgas360.com/tag/investors/), [oil markets](https://www.oilandgas360.com/tag/oil-markets/), [OPEC](https://www.oilandgas360.com/tag/opec/), [shale revolution](https://www.oilandgas360.com/tag/shale-revolution/)

(By Oil & Gas 360) – For much of the past decade, oil markets were defined by abundance. The U.S. shale revolution, ample OPEC+ spare capacity, and slowing demand growth encouraged investors to focus on production, inventories, and macroeconomic trends. Geopolitical events still generated headlines, but price spikes were often short-lived as markets assumed disrupted supplies could be replaced and trade flows rerouted.

That assumption is beginning to change.

Crude oil recently posted its biggest weekly gain in months as renewed hostilities between the United States and Iran reignited concerns over energy security and the possibility of disruptions to global shipping. Nationwide fuel shortages are beginning to put pressure on Russia’s agricultural sector, despite directives from President Vladimir Putin to guarantee farmers enough supplies for the harvest and planting seasons, Agriculture Minister Oksana Lut [said](https://www.interfax.ru/russia/1103832 "said") Friday.

“There are rough patches on the ground, and we’ll work through them with each specific region and business as needed,” Lut said at a farming forum in Siberia.

She cited a [directive](http://en.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/80174 "directive") issued by Putin last month ordering a strict fuel delivery schedule for farms to counter the impact of Ukrainian strikes on oil refineries. Despite the current bottlenecks, Lut expressed confidence that these deliveries would ultimately be completed in full.

# Chicago wheat gains for the third week in a row on Black Sea concerns

Posted to [Maritime Reporter](/blogs/blogs-maritime_reporter) on July 16, 2026

Chicago wheat slipped on 'Friday, but continued to rise for the third week in a row. This was due to concerns about disruptions of exports out of 'the Black Sea Region as supplies tighten up in Europe and North America. Profit-taking caused the most-active Chicago Board of Trade wheat contract to slip 0.89%, or $6.68-3/4 per bushel, by 0200 GMT. However the contract was still up 4.45% on the week. Analysts say that the Kerch Strait was closed after strikes in Ukraine and that the deteriorating conditions of U.S. crops have supported prices. Summary

* US lawmakers said memory chips from China’s **CXMT** and **YMTC** pose an unacceptable risk to **US security and supply chain security**, and urged a ban on purchases of the products in the US.
* The lawmakers called for **CXMT** and **YMTC** to face tighter restrictions through the Commerce Department’s **export control list**, while also urging **joint action with South Korea, Japan and the EU**.
